author: Mark Atwood
text:
Per workspace AGENTS.md 'Canonical Templates' rule, adding an auth-contract doc block to FileNodeBackend would diverge from the canonical jmap-mail-server (which has no such block on its MailBackend trait). The bead's own 'Propagation note' says: 'Every extension-server in the workspace shares this concern... Apply the same depth of contract spec across the sibling family in a single sweep.'

Two options:

(a) Do filenode-server only now. Accept the divergence as a forward-propagation debt; file a follow-up sweep bead for the other 6 extension-server siblings (mail, chat, calendars, tasks, contacts, sharing, metadata).

(b) File a workspace-wide propagation epic. Add the auth-contract doc block to mail-server (canonical) first, then propagate to filenode-server and the other 5 siblings in the same pass. JMAP-510h.44 becomes a child of that epic.

Recommendation: (b). The bead author explicitly called for a workspace sweep, and option (a) creates immediate debt that future contributors will trip on (they will see one trait with the block, six without, and have to guess which is the model). The /do-beads session was invoked with --epic JMAP-510h, so the workspace-wide work exceeds this session's scope; filing the epic and parking this bead under it is the right move.

Note: I verified mail-server's src/backend.rs trait doc (lines 44-54) does NOT have an auth-contract block — only an 'isUnread convention' header at the module level. The bead's premise (mail-server has its own pass) refers to the isUnread block, which is not an auth-contract block. So the gap is workspace-wide, including on the canonical.

The decision needs human judgment because: (i) it determines whether this bead lives or is superseded by an epic; (ii) it commits the workspace to a 7-crate sweep at minimum; (iii) the bead is correct that the gap is real, but the scope is bigger than the bead's filename.
